injuryReport.name: Tony Adams
injuryReport.beatComment: Adams was added to the Titans' injury report right before the 1 p.m. ET kickoff due to the illness, and the veteran safety wasn't able to take any snaps before being ruled out for Sunday's contest. Terrell Burgess drew the start at safety alongside Kevin Winston in Adams' absence, per Terry McCormick of TitanInsider.com.

injuryReport.name: Nicholas Singleton
injuryReport.beatComment: Week 11 marks the fifth time in six games that Singleton will be a healthy scratch, despite the fact that Tyjae Spears (knee) was placed on injured reserve Saturday. As such, Michael Carter and Julius Chestnut will operate as the Titans' rotational options in the backfield behind workhorse running back Tony Pollard on Sunday. Singleton's next opportunity to play is Week 12 against the Jaguars on Nov. 29.

injuryReport.name: Cor'Dale Flott
injuryReport.beatComment: Flott was hurt with just under six minutes remaining in the first half while tackling CeeDee Lamb. He was evaluated on the sideline and subsequently deemed questionable to return. Micah Robinson entered at cornerback in Flott's stead.

injuryReport.name: Terrell Burgess
injuryReport.beatComment: Burgess injured his knee early in the second half, and he will be sidelined for the rest of Sunday's contest. He was filling in for Tony Adams (illness) at safety, so Isaiah Oliver is the next man up for the Titans.

injuryReport.name: Dan Moore Jr.
injuryReport.beatComment: Moore may have picked up the injury during the third quarter, and he's being evaluated by medical staff to determine whether he can return. James Hudson figures to take over at left tackle in Moore's absence.

irReserve.name: Jaylen Harrell
irReserve.beatComment: Harrell is being monitored following Saturday's accident. The third-year pro tore his ACL in a preseason game against the 49ers in mid-August, which led to him being placed on season-ending injured reserve.

irReserve.name: Tyjae Spears
irReserve.beatComment: Spears was sidelined for Weeks 7 and 8 due to a knee injury but was cleared to play against the Jaguars in Week 10, when he turned four carries into 28 yards and failed to haul in his lone target. He was initially listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Cowboys after logging a full practice Friday, but the Titans have determined that a stint on injured reserve is warranted for the fourth-year running back. Spears will be required to miss at least the next four games, so his next chance to play is Week 15 against the Colts on Sunday, Dec. 20. Tony Pollard will continue to be the workhorse running back for the Titans while Julius Chestnut and rookie fifth-rounder Nicholas Singleton provide depth out of the backfield.

coachingMatchup.headline: Liam Coen & DC Anthony Campanile vs. HC Robert Saleh & DC Gus Bradley (EverBank Stadium)
coachingMatchup.summary: Week 12 two-sided coordinator chess match pitting Jacksonville Jaguars's staff (Liam Coen, OC Grant Udinski, DC Anthony Campanile) against Tennessee Titans (1-9)—testing both Jacksonville's offensive efficiency and its defensive pass-rush and coverage discipline.
bullets: Pass-Game Efficiency & Coverage Shell Delta: Liam Coen and OC Grant Udinski look to stress Tennessee Titans's single-high vs. two-high rotations with pre-snap motion, spacing, and play-action timing, while Tennessee Titans's defensive front and coverage disguises aim to compress intermediate throwing windows.

Trench Run-Fit & Two-Way Leverage: DC Anthony Campanile balances pass-rush pressure with two-high/split-safety discipline on early downs, while Tennessee Titans's offense tests Jacksonville's edge containment, third-down execution, and red-zone stops.
